title: Smooth a cake's side: hold the smoother still as the other arm turns the turntable
instruction: Smooth the side of the cake on the turntable. With one gripper, take the smoother from its stand by the handle and hold it still and upright, its blade against the cake's side, its bottom edge just above the turntable. With the other gripper, turn the turntable anticlockwise (seen from above) by its black pegs almost a full turn. Then move the smoother 1 cm from the cake and both grippers 2 cm from the pegs. Never touch the cake with a gripper or its top with the smoother.
context: Cake decorators in commercial and supermarket bakeries (O*NET 51-3011.00 Bakers) finish an iced cake's side by holding a bench scraper or cake smoother still against it, upright, flat on the side or angled up to about 45 degrees with its edge doing the work, its bottom edge on or just above the turntable, while the other hand turns the turntable: the tool stays put and the cake moves under it, as on a potter's wheel or a lathe (a tool moved round the cake leaves ridges). As a robot task this is asymmetric two-arm control: one arm holds a light tool a millimetre or two from a moving surface, within 10 mm and 4 degrees of where it was set, for about 40 s, while the other turns the work nearly a full turn in hand-over-hand strokes on its pegs. The score is the share of the side that passed the still tool while the other gripper turned the turntable.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four things are on the table. (1) Cake turntable, fixed in place, its vertical axis at x 27.0 cm, y -5.0 cm: a grey cast-aluminium base disc 100 mm across and 5 mm tall fixed to the table and, on it, a white HDPE plate 340 mm across and 10 mm thick (its top 15 mm above the table) that turns about the axis with a bearing drag of 0.10 N m s per radian (let go spinning at 1 rad/s it stops within 6 degrees; no spring, no detent) and has a lug under it that meets a fixed stop pin 11.5 degrees clockwise and 349.5 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) of where it starts. Fixed on the plate and turning with it: a dummy iced cake, a cream-coloured rigid foam cylinder 120 mm across and 50 mm tall centred on the axis (its top 65 mm above the table); four black acetal pegs, cylinders 20 mm across and 30 mm tall, their centres 155 mm from the axis at 30, 120, 210 and 300 degrees at the start (angles anticlockwise from straight forward, +x); and a red vinyl index mark 20 x 8 mm, 1 mm thick, 155 mm out at 0 degrees. Plate, cake and pegs weigh 0.93 kg together. (2) Cake smoother, loose, 67 g: a clear acrylic blade 100 mm long, 6 mm thick and 70 mm tall (50 g) with a hollow black polypropylene handle (2 mm walls, 17 g) 70 mm long, 32 mm wide and 30 mm tall centred along its top edge (100 mm tall in all). It starts hanging by its handle in the stand, its length along x, the blade's centre at x 27.0 cm, y +21.5 cm, its bottom edge 2 mm above the table. (3) and (4) Smoother stand: two grey ABS blocks, each 120 mm along x, 12 mm wide and 72 mm tall, fixed to the table side by side 18 mm apart, centred at x 27.0 cm, y +23.0 cm and y +20.0 cm; the blade hangs in the slot between them (6 mm clear each side) and the handle rests across both blocks' tops (7 mm on each). Gripping from above, only the left arm reaches the stand. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the turntable's angle (0 at the start, anticlockwise seen from above), the smoother's pose and each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open: 94 mm). A gripper's 'finger zone' is the round zone about its axis from the finger tips 38 mm up, reaching the fingers' outer corners (half the gap plus their 10 mm thickness, and half their 40 mm width). The smoother is 'held' when a gripper at most half open has its finger-tip point within 10 mm of the handle. It is 'set' when it is held, tilted less than 5 degrees, the blade's lowest point is 1 mm below to 5 mm above the plate's top, the blade comes within -1 to +3 mm of the cake's side where they are nearest (the 'contact point'; negative: pressed in) with its length within 45 degrees of the side's tangent there (flat on the side, or angled with an edge on it), and it is still: the blade's centre moving slower than 1 cm/s and within 10 mm of where it was when the smoother was put in place, its heading turning slower than 3 degrees/s and within 4 degrees of its heading then. Out of either window, it is not set again until taken away (its centre 20 mm or more from where it was put, its bottom 20 mm or more above the plate, or let go). The side is 360 one-degree sectors fixed to the cake. While the smoother stays set and the other gripper (not the one holding it) has its finger zone within 5 mm of a peg, each control step's turn of the turntable, less any part of it the blade's centre followed round, carries the side across both edges of the credited arc, 3 degrees either side of the contact point: every sector an edge crosses has passed the blade, once (steps counting under 0.01 or turning over 20 degrees are ignored). So moving the smoother, dragging or twisting the cake round with it, or a turntable coasting with no gripper at a peg adds nothing; one uninterrupted turn of D degrees under a still smoother passes D + 6 sectors (one more at either end). The stop allows 349.5 degrees of turn, so the full score asks for 340 of the 360. Score 0 if at any moment a finger zone comes within 5 mm of the cake (side or top), any part of the smoother is less than 3 mm above the cake's top within 57 mm of its axis seen from above, or the smoother's lowest point is 20 mm or more below the table top (it fell off). Otherwise: 1.0 if 340 or more sectors have passed the blade and then, for 1 s, the smoother is 10 mm or more from the cake, every finger zone 20 mm or more from every peg and the turntable turning slower than 0.05 rad/s; 0.75 if 270 or more (or 340 without that finish); 0.5 if 180 or more; 0.25 if the smoother was set for 1 s without a break; 0 otherwise. The score is read at the last step; the trial ends once 1.0 has held for 1 s. Grippers that cannot be read hold nothing, turn nothing and miss the finish (finger zones then unchecked). In a real trial: the angle from a degree ring on the rim on video, the gap with 1 mm and 3 mm shims, the height with a 5 mm shim, stillness against two pointers on stands off the plate, the grippers from logged joint states.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The turntable is one fixed articulation: plate, cake and pegs on one revolute joint with 0.10 N m s/rad of damping and stops at -0.2 and 6.1 rad; the smoother is one rigid body (its 67 g spread over its shapes by volume). No icing is simulated: the dummy cake is rigid and smoothing is scored from geometry (gap, height, stillness, turn). Real turntables are turned by the rim; the pegs give a top-down gripper a hold.
reset_notes: Turn the plate back to its start: the red index mark straight forward, the pegs at 30, 120, 210 and 300 degrees anticlockwise from forward. Hang the smoother back in its stand by the handle, its length along x, the blade centred at x 27.0 cm, y +21.5 cm. The turntable and the stand are fixed; nothing is consumed (in a real build, wipe the dummy cake's side if the blade marked it).
